Previous history included symptomatic Hashimoto /C213s thyroiditis. Although initial thyroid stimulating hormone was elevated and free thyroxine reduced, these remained stable with thyroxine replacement. Type 1 diabetes mellitus was diagnosed following presentation with diabetic ketoacidosis. Other complaints included lower limb myoclonic jerks and post-prandial abdominal cramps with dyspepsia. Antiglutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) antibody was positive with a titre of 87 U/ml (range 0–1 U/ml). Antinuclear antibody was positive with a speckled pattern (titre: 1/640). Antipancreatic islet cell, anti-adrenal cortex, antitissue transglutaminase and anti-endomysial antibodies were positive. Antithyroid peroxidase antibody was positive (titre: >1000 U/ml). Duodenal biopsy demonstrated villous atrophy.
